chunks: Yes, by Allah, they had heard it and understood it
but the world appeared glittering in their eyes and its embellishments seduced them!
Behold, by Him who split the grain (to grow) and created living beings,
if people had not come to me and supporters had not exhausted the argument,
and if there had been no pledge of Allah with the learned to the effect that they should not acquiesce in the gluttony of the oppressor and the hunger of the oppressed,
I would have cast the rope of Caliphate on its own shoulders, and would have given the last one the same treatment as to the first one.
Then you would have seen that in my view this world of yours is no better than the sneezing of a goat.

key_terms.عَفْطَةِ عَنز: sneezing of a goat (metaphor for something trivial)
key_terms.فَلَقَ الْحَبَّةَ: split the grain (referring to Allah's creative power)

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali (AS) delay taking the Caliphate according to the Shaqshaqiya sermon?
ai.summary: In this pivotal passage from the *Shaqshaqiya Sermon*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) attributes the delay in his caliphate not to a lack of right, but to the companions' attachment to worldly power, metaphorically described as 'Zibrīj' (gold or fine fabric). He invokes the scholarly covenant (*'ahd al-'ulama'*) to remain silent in the face of the oppressor's satiety and the oppressed's hunger as the primary constraint, while also alluding to the 'presence of the presenters' (*ḥuḍūr al--ḥāḍir*)—often interpreted as the arrival of the Prophet's companions or the consensus of the elite—which prevented him from seizing power immediately and decisively.
